correctness.rationale: For every complex 2x2 T, the exact Pauli representation gives ||Re(e^{-iθ}T)||=|sθ|+||qθ||. Integrating its square and evaluating H²+K² reduces the lower equality to triangle equality for vectors sθqθ; either trace zero or phase-real Hermitian, with the affine-line argument establishing necessity. Equality of angular squared average with its maximum requires constant f; trace nonzero yields a noncancelable cusp, while traceless constant f implies T²=0. All boundaries including T=0 are covered. The actual packaged checker passes 1200 numerical matrix-family tests, supplementary not proof.

value.rationale: A complete equality classification of two natural sharp estimates for a new integrated numerical-radius norm closes the first nontrivial full-matrix case. It detects an unexpected broad rank-two lower sharpness class (traceless invertible matrices) absent from the source’s examples, separates this from phase-Hermitian equality, and proves square-zero as the sole upper-sharpness mechanism. It also yields a simple exact Hilbert–Schmidt identity on the entire traceless matrix subspace. The result is restricted to dimension two and makes no unsupported broader consequence claim.
